name: Primary Mediastinal Large B-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of a bulky anterior mediastinal mass on imaging
Histological confirmation of large B-cell lymphoma with characteristic features including sclerosis and compartmentalizing fibrosis
Immunophenotypic profile showing CD20+, CD30+, CD23+ expression with absence of surface immunoglobulin
Exclusion of other diffuse large B-cell lymphoma subtypes and mediastinal gray zone lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of large B-cell lymphoma with typical immunophenotype and presence of a bulky anterior mediastinal mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, radiological, histopathological, and immunophenotypic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bulky anterior mediastinal mass causing superior vena cava syndrome
pathognomonic.notes: Compression of superior vena cava leading to facial swelling and venous distension
searchTerms: mass causing superior vena cava syndrome

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging mediastinal mass detected on imaging

common.notes: Shortness of breath from tracheal or bronchial compression
searchTerms: shortness of breath from airway pressure
breathing difficulty due to airway compression

common.notes: Due to mass effect or pleural involvement

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

occasional.notes: Venous congestion from superior vena cava syndrome

searchTerms: trouble swallowing due to food pipe blockage

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to anemia or systemic illness

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms from spinal cord compression
searchTerms: weakness or numbness from spinal tumor
blood clot in superior vena cava
superior vena cava blockage by clot

imaging: CT scan showing bulky anterior mediastinal mass
PET-CT demonstrating high FDG uptake in mediastinal mass
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD30, CD23
Histopathology showing large atypical B-cells with sclerosis

distinguishingFeatures: Shares features of PMBCL and classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Mixed immunophenotype with CD15 and CD30 positivity

redFlags: Rapidly progressive superior vena cava syndrome
Severe respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
Unexplained persistent B symptoms with mediastinal mass
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Savage KJ. Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. Blood. 2014;123(8):1187-1193.
Zinzani PL, et al. Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma: current treatment approaches and future perspectives. Expert Rev Hematol. 2019;12(5):383-392.
